title.narrative: Climate Resilient Agriculture: transforming livelihoods of 61,570 poor women, men and children Kenya

description.narrative: The project will be implement in three year and aims to achieve improved livelihoods security for 61,570 poor women, men and children from hazard-prone and/or marginalised rural communities in Kitui, Marsabit and Maralal in Kenya, through an integrated approach that: increases the productivity and resilience of agricultural systems; consolidates engagement in markets and diversified income generation; strengthens adaptation to climate change; and increases the ability of local, small scale food producers to access services and influence development practices. There are four interrelated project outcomes namely: 1. Small-holder farmer households are using sustainable and agro-ecological practices Kitui- Kenya 2. Small holder farmer households engaging in local markets in Kitui, Marasabit and Maralal - Kenya 3. Communities Kitui, Marasabit and Maralal -Kenya have increased capacity to manage risks 4. Learn and capture the best practice and use to inform and influence climate resilient development policy and practices by CAFOD and partners The proposed project fits with the CAFOD East Africa Regional Strategy in that it is an integrated project. In the current strategy integration is the main focus. Additionally, the project focuses on food security that include accessibility, availability, stability and affordability while integrating key components on disaster risk reduction, climate change adaptation and governance which are core components of the East Africa strategy. Poor Women, men and children living in remote and hazard-prone rural areas in Kitui, Marsabit and Maralal - Kenya rely on smallholder agriculture to provide their main source of food or income. Despite macro-economic growth in Kenya communities are unable to maintain a basic standard of living. Poverty is widespread (MDG1), many face food insecurity, and livelihoods are highly dependent on climatic conditions. The most recent research has found that there is high probability that climate change will exacerbate the vulnerability of agricultural systems particularly in regions of Africa, (Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, 2014 5th Report, in Kenya, prolonged periods of drought are common (National Climate Change Response Strategy, 2010). CAFOD has significant experience of working in Kitui, Marsabit and Maralal in these areas there exist clear constrains that hinder people from realising a sustainable livelihood exemplifying the need for the proposed action. These constrains include: Limited adaptation in agricultural systems, Limited livelihood options, Constraints within the market systems, Vulnerability to risk and Limited Voice and Influence. The project support is from DFID and CAFOD appeal under match Fund III.
